key_insight: AI research in medical imaging grew rapidly from 2017-2025, with the UK producing a smaller share of papers but achieving relatively high citation impact and a shift toward generative and foundation-based methods.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest AI-enabled imaging tools are becoming more influential in research and may increasingly shape reconstruction, synthesis, and diagnostic workflows, though translation to routine care still depends on validation and implementation quality.
method: Scopus bibliometric analysis of AI-related medical imaging publications from 2017-2025
Compared global output with a UK-affiliated subset using TP, TC, CPP, and growth trends
Mapped co-authorship and keyword networks with VOSviewer to identify collaboration and thematic clusters
evidence_signal: The dataset included 13,452 global publications with 194,650 citations, and 889 UK-affiliated papers with a higher CPP (21.00) than the global average (14.47).
watch_item: Recent years may show a citation-lag effect, so newer generative and foundation-model papers may be undercounted in impact despite growing activity.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging With Emphasis on Generative and Foundation-Based Methods: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global and United Kingdom Research, 2017-2025
